svg.title: Speed against gradient, next to hill-race records
svg.desc: Speed as a multiple of flat speed from a 30 per cent descent to a 20 per cent climb. Kay's 2012 curve fitted to hill-race records rises to 1.23 times flat at 10 per cent down, then turns over and falls below flat speed by 30 per cent down. Runsketch's elite curve tracks it within 0.015 all the way down and its recreational curve sits below, with a shaded band covering the beginner-to-elite spread that closes at zero. Uphill all Runsketch levels are identical, reaching 0.736 at a 10 per cent climb against the records' 0.651. Fake My Stats plateaus at 1.40 on every descent steeper than 10 per cent, and Dibma plateaus at 1.176 downhill and floors at 0.667 above a 15 per cent climb where the records reach 0.421. SimuRun and fakemy.run have no gradient term and sit at exactly 1.0 everywhere.
